message.content:
Below is a quick‑look list of the most common “long‑weekend” holidays that Canadians typically enjoy in 2023.  
(These are the federal holidays that fall on a Friday or a Monday, creating a three‑day weekend.  Some provinces have additional holidays that may also produce long weekends.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Weekend Span |
|---------|-------------|--------------|
| **Family Day** (Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario) | Monday, Feb 20 | Feb 18–20 |
| **Good Friday** | Friday, Apr 7 | Apr 7–9 |
| **Victoria Day** (most provinces) | Monday, May 22 | May 20–22 |
| **Labour Day** | Monday, Sep 4 | Sep 2–4 |
| **Thanksgiving** | Monday, Oct 9 | Oct 7–9 |
| **Remembrance Day** (most provinces) | Monday, Nov 11 | Nov 9–11 |
| **Christmas** | Monday, Dec 25 | Dec 23–25 |

> **Note:**  
> • New Year’s Day (Sunday, Jan 1) and Canada Day (Saturday, Jul 1) do not create a long weekend in 2023.  
> • Some provinces observe additional holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, or the Civic Holiday in Ontario) that can also create long weekends.  

If you need a province‑specific list or want to pull this data programmatically, you can use a holiday‑API such as [Calendarific](https://calendarific.com/) or the [Date.nager.at](https://date.nager.at/) service. They return JSON with holiday dates, which you can then filter for Fridays/Mondays to generate your own long‑weekend list.
